results.title: Five Structural Biases in Neurofeedback-for-ADHD Research: Why the Evidence Look
results.reason: This paper directly addresses a clinical intervention (neurofeedback) for ADHD, examining methodological issues in research that impact clinical practice relevance. It focuses on assessment, diagnosis, and intervention evaluation - all core clinical psychology topics.

results.title: Self-regulation, psychological well-being, and stress at university: A mixed-met
results.reason: This study focuses on university students' self-regulation, well-being, and stress, which falls under educational psychology rather than clinical psychology. While there are psychological elements, the population (students) and context (university setting) are not directly relevant to clinical practice with patients/clients. The study examines academic stress rather than clinical psychopathology or therapeutic interventions.

results.title: Psychosocial and Masculinity-Related Predictors of Suicide Risk Among Male Unive
results.reason: The study examines suicide risk factors among male university students, which is highly relevant to clinical psychology practice, particularly for suicidality assessment and prevention interventions.
results.authors: Aisling McGrath; Shane O'Donnell; Noel Richardson

results.reason: The study examines dog ownership's impact on physical activity and wellbeing in individuals with severe mental illness, which is directly relevant to clinical psychology practice for managing chronic psychiatric conditions.

results.title: Personalized Machine Learning Models for Predicting Panic Attacks
results.reason: The paper focuses on machine learning models for predicting panic attacks using wearable technology, which falls under AI/tech and digital health rather than clinical psychology practice. While panic attacks are a clinical topic, the primary emphasis is on algorithm development and prediction rather than therapy, assessment, diagnosis, or clinical intervention for practicing clinicians.
